title: ulmus glabra var. pendula
intro: Ulmus glabra var. pendula, commonly known as Weeping Elm, is a deciduous tree characterized by its slender branches that droop downwards, creating a weeping effect. The Weeping Elm is valued for its health benefits, including the ability to reduce fever, inflammation, and cough, as well as its antiseptic and astringent properties. The therapeutic actions of Ulmus glabra var. pendula include its use as an expectorant, demulcent, and emollient to soothe mucous membranes and promote the healing of wounds. The bioactive constituents of this plant include flavonoids, tannins, and phenolic acids, which contribute to its medicinal properties.
